title: Active join-boundary criterion for a weak operadic colimit
statement: Use the simplicial sets, quasicategories and spaces of [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones], joins of [def-coef-infinity-relative-cone], and active arrows and weak operadic colimits of [def-coef-operadic-correspondence]. Let $p:\mathcal V^\otimes\to\Delta^{\mathrm{op}}$ be a monoidal infinity category and $K$ a small simplicial set. Write $\Delta^{\mathrm{op}}_{\mathrm{act}}$ for the wide subcategory of $\Delta^{\mathrm{op}}$ whose arrows are opposite to endpoint-preserving maps. The active subcategories retain all objects and exactly the arrows over these active maps. Let $c:K^{\triangleright}\to\mathcal V^\otimes_{\mathrm{act}}$ be an active cocone; its apex can be a tuple of any length. Then $c$ is weakly operadically colimiting if and only if the following boundary-lifting condition holds. For every $d>0$, every map $u:K\star\partial\Delta^d\to\mathcal V^\otimes_{\mathrm{act}}$ whose restriction to $K\star\{0\}$ is $c$ and whose value $u(d)$ lies in $\mathcal V=\mathcal V^\otimes_{[1]}$, and every specified extension $a:K\star\Delta^d\to\Delta^{\mathrm{op}}_{\mathrm{act}}$ of $pu$, there is $\widetilde u:K\star\Delta^d\to\mathcal V^\otimes_{\mathrm{act}}$ with $\widetilde u|_{K\star\partial\Delta^d}=u$ and $p\widetilde u=a$. All restrictions are equalities of simplicial maps. No colimits of other shapes and no tensor preservation hypotheses are assumed; $K$ is allowed to be empty.

source.place: Proposition 3.1.1.7, printed pp. 319–321; the nonsymmetric active-coslice definition is GH Definition A.2.1 and Remark A.2.2. Nonsymmetric formulation following Gepner–Haugseng, arXiv:1312.3178v4 Appendix A. Read online; archive WANTED. No Stacks tag states this infinity-categorical fact.

proof.text: Put $B=N(\Delta^{\mathrm{op}}_{\mathrm{act}})$, $C=\mathcal V^\otimes\times_{N(\Delta^{\mathrm{op}})}B$, $T=c|_K$, and $v=c(*)$. The monoidal projection is an inner fibration, so its pullback $q:C\to B$ is an inner fibration and $C$ is a quasicategory. Here $B$ is the nerve of a category, whose inner horns fill by composition; lifting first to $B$ and then to $C$ proves the assertion. The object $[1]$ is terminal in $\Delta^{\mathrm{op}}_{\mathrm{act}}$: the opposite endpoint-preserving map $[1]\to[r]$ must send $0$ to $0$ and $1$ to $r$, including $r=0$. Thus any simplex all of whose vertices are colors projects constantly to $[1]$, and a cone from any fixed base diagram to a color has a unique base extension. Define $X=C_{T/}$ and $Y=B_{qT/}$ by their join simplices. Apply the relative-coslice lemma with $K_0=\varnothing$ to factor $Q:X\to Y$ as a left fibration $X\to C\times_B Y$ followed by the pullback of $q$. Both factors are inner fibrations, and filling successively proves that $Q$ is an inner fibration. The same lemma with target the point says that $C_{h/}\to C$ is a left fibration for every fixed diagram $h$. These constructions are made in a containing universe, so no size change or colimit existence is implicit.

source.place: Proposition 3.1.1.7, coslice setup; nonsymmetric base from GH Definition A.2.1.

proof.text: For $h=T,c$ put $Z_h=\mathcal V\times_C C_{h/}$ and let $\psi:Z_c\to Z_T$ be restriction. The relative-coslice lemma with $q:C\to\Delta^0$ and $K\hookrightarrow K^{\triangleright}$ proves that $\psi$ is a left fibration; its restriction to color apices is a pullback. Both $Z_h\to\mathcal V$ are left fibrations as well. The join-slice comparison identifies their fibers at $w\in\mathcal V$ with the spaces of coherent cocones on $h$ with apex $w$, naturally in $h$ and its restrictions. In particular the fiber for $T$ is the active-cocone space in the definition of weak operadic colimit. To identify the fiber for $c$, let $A=K^{\triangleright}$ and take the target-fixed arrow right fibration $E_w\to C$. Its sections over $h:L\to C$ are exactly the fixed-source, fixed-target arrow transformations $h\to\Delta_Lw$, by currying. Taking $\varnothing\hookrightarrow K$ in the cone-monomorphism lemma makes $\{*\}\hookrightarrow A$ right anodyne. Right-fibration exponentiation, pulled back to the fixed diagram $c$, therefore makes evaluation $\Gamma_c(E_w)\to\Gamma_v(E_w)$ a trivial Kan fibration. It is a weak homotopy equivalence by the Kan model theorem. The join-slice comparison, for $A$ and for the point, now identifies this map with the apex restriction $Z_c(w)\to\operatorname{Map}_C(v,w)$ up to its natural equivalences. All these comparisons commute with restriction to $K$. Write $e_w:Z_c(w)\to\operatorname{Map}_C(v,w)$ for this apex equivalence and $c^*$ for composition with $c$ into the coherent $T$-cocone space. After the stated comparisons, naturality gives $\psi_w\simeq c^*e_w$, including the higher coherences. Since $e_w$ is an equivalence, the defining mapping-space condition and two-out-of-three show that $c$ is weakly operadically colimiting if and only if every fiber map $\psi_w$ is a weak homotopy equivalence.

source.place: GH Definition A.2.1 and Remark A.2.2, mapping-space interpretation; general cone comparisons expanded using the cited statements.

proof.text: The fiber condition of Step 2 is equivalent to $\psi$ being a trivial Kan fibration. For the forward implication, classify $Z_c\to\mathcal V$ and $Z_T\to\mathcal V$ by space-valued transport. The map $\psi$ corresponds to a coherent transformation with precisely these fiber maps as its components. The componentwise equivalence criterion makes this transformation an equivalence. The mapping-space and composition compatibility of transport supplies an inverse map over $\mathcal V$, with inverse homotopies in the Kan complexes of maps over $\mathcal V$. The inverse homotopies are therefore equivalence edges after forgetting the base, so $\psi$ is a functor equivalence of total quasicategories. Since $\psi$ is a left fibration, the left-fibration equivalence-lifting lemma makes it an isofibration; the Joyal characterization makes it a Joyal fibration and a Joyal weak equivalence. The weak factorization system in the Joyal model structure then gives lifting against every monomorphism, in particular every boundary, including dimension zero. This is a trivial Kan fibration. Conversely, each fiber map of a trivial Kan fibration is again a trivial Kan fibration: a boundary lifting square in a pullback is the same square upstairs with its fixed base coordinate. The Kan model theorem makes each such map a weak homotopy equivalence, giving Step 2's condition. This proves both implications without identifying arbitrary categorical equivalences with strict-fiber equivalences.

source.place: GH Remark A.2.2 / HA Remark 3.1.1.5; the fiberwise-to-total argument is written out.

proof.text: Assume now that $c$ is weakly operadically colimiting, and fix the specified boundary $u$ and base extension $a$ in dimension $d>0$. Under the degreewise join formula these are a map $U:\partial\Delta^d\to X$ and a map $A:\Delta^d\to Y$ with $QU=A|_{\partial\Delta^d}$; $U(0)=c$ and the apex of $U(d)$ is a color $w$. Define the monotone map $r:[d]\times[1]\to[d]$ by $r(i,0)=i$ and $r(i,1)=d$. Inside $P=\Delta^d\times\Delta^1$ set $W=(\partial\Delta^d\times\{0\})\cup(\Lambda_d^d\times\Delta^1)\cup(\Delta^d\times\{1\})$. Its image under $r$ lies in $\partial\Delta^d$: every simplex of $\Lambda_d^d$ omits some vertex $j<d$, and applying $r$ can add only the vertex $d$, so it still omits $j$; on the bottom boundary $r$ is the identity and on the top row it is constant. Thus $g_0=U(r|_W)$ is defined and lies over the prescribed map $Ar:P\to Y$. It is constant with value $U(d)$ on the top row, and $g_0(0,0)=c$. A lift over the entire prism, restricted to its bottom row, gives exactly the required filler of $U$ over $A$. The join degree formula turns its two exact restriction equations into those requested for $\widetilde u$.

source.place: Proposition 3.1.1.7, contraction setup; elementary calculation of the domain and its restriction.

proof.text: Enlarge $W$ first by the $d$ simplices $b_i:\Delta^d\to P$ ($1\leq i\leq d$), whose vertex $j$ is $(j,0)$ for $j\leq d-i$ and $(j-1,1)$ for $j>d-i$. Put $t=d-i$; its two blocks are $(0,0),\ldots,(t,0)$ and $(t,1),\ldots,(d-1,1)$. Deleting position $j<t$ or $j>t+1$ omits a first coordinate less than $d$, so that face lies in $\Lambda_d^d\times\Delta^1\subset W$. Deleting position $t+1$ gives a bottom-row boundary face when $i=1$, and for $i>1$ gives the face of $b_{i-1}$ obtained by deleting its last bottom vertex. Deleting position $t$ gives $(0,0),\ldots,(t-1,0),(t,1),\ldots,(d-1,1)$. If $t>0$, this face is mixed and has every first coordinate $0,\ldots,d-1$, hence is not in $W$; it is in no earlier $b_h$, since $h<i$ implies $d-h>t$, whereas the displayed face contains $(t,1)$. Every proper subface of this missing face lies in another codimension-one face. Thus, for $i<d$, the old intersection is exactly $\Lambda_t^d$, with $0<t<d$, and the inner fibration $Q$ fills the cell over the fixed map $Ar$. For $i=d$, $t=0$, the formerly missing face is entirely in the top row, so the old intersection is the full $\partial\Delta^d$. Keep this last boundary for Step 6. When $d=1$ there are no inner cells in this phase and both endpoints of $b_1$ are already present. In every case $b_i$ itself is new: it is mixed with all first coordinates $0,\ldots,d-1$, and an earlier cell has no upper vertex $(t,1)$.

source.place: Proposition 3.1.1.7, first prism filtration, with its final attachment made explicit.

proof.text: The remaining first-phase cell $b_d$ has vertices $(0,0),(0,1),\ldots,(d-1,1)$. Its first vertex is $c$ in $X$; its other vertices, with all intervening simplices on that face, form the constant diagram with value $U(d)$, whose apex is $w\in\mathcal V$. Under associativity of the ordered join, its full boundary over $X$ therefore consists of a map $\partial\Delta^{d-1}\to Z_c$ together with its prescribed extension $\Delta^{d-1}\to Z_T$. Indeed $\Delta^d=\{0\}\star\Delta^{d-1}$, and the two parts of its boundary are the face without $0$ and $\{0\}\star\partial\Delta^{d-1}$. This is precisely a boundary lifting problem for $\psi$. Step 3 fills it, also when $d-1=0$. It fills the cell over $Ar$: all its vertices after the first lie over $[1]$, so the terminality calculation in Step 1 makes its base extension from $qc$ unique. We have now extended $g_0$ across all $b_i$ with its old values fixed.

source.place: Proposition 3.1.1.7, exceptional first-phase cell; GH Remark A.2.2 gives precisely this lifting property.

proof.text: Finally adjoin, in the order $k=1,\ldots,d+1$, the maximal prism simplices $s_k:\Delta^{d+1}\to P$ with $s_k(j)=(j,0)$ for $j<k$ and $s_k(j)=(j-1,1)$ for $j\geq k$. Deleting a position $j<k-1$, or $k<j<d+1$, omits a first coordinate less than $d$, so that face lies in $W$. Deleting position $k-1$ gives the top row when $k=1$, and for $k>1$ gives the face of $s_{k-1}$ with its first upper vertex removed. If $k\leq d$, deleting the last position $d+1$ gives $b_{d-k+1}$, already attached. The remaining face, obtained by deleting position $k$, is $(0,0),\ldots,(k-1,0),(k,1),\ldots,(d,1)$. For $k\leq d$ it is mixed with all first coordinates, so not in $W$, and its upper vertex $(d,1)$ excludes every $b_i$. Its bottom vertex $(k-1,0)$ excludes every earlier $s_l$, whose bottom block stops at $l-1<k-1$. For $k=d+1$ the remaining face is the entire bottom simplex, also absent from $W$ and all earlier cells because they omit $(d,0)$. Consequently each old intersection is exactly $\Lambda_k^{d+1}$; all proper subfaces of its missing face belong to another face. For $k\leq d$ this horn is inner, and $Q$ fills it over $Ar$. For $k=d+1$, the last edge is $(d,0)\to(d,1)$, already in $\Lambda_d^d\times\Delta^1\subset W$. Its image under $r$ is the degenerate edge at $d$, so its image in $X$ under $g_0$ is a degenerate edge, an equivalence. The equivalence-edge outer-horn lemma, in dimension $d+1\geq2$, fills the final horn over $Ar$. The $s_k$ exhaust $P$: each maximal chain of $[d]\times[1]$ uses every first coordinate and changes its second coordinate exactly once, at $k-1$ for exactly one $k$. Every chain extends to a maximal chain. Restriction to the bottom row gives the requested $\widetilde u$ as in Step 4. No equivalence condition on an original boundary arrow was used.

source.place: Proposition 3.1.1.7, second prism filtration and final outer horn.

proof.text: Conversely, assume the boundary condition in the statement. Take any boundary lifting problem for $\psi$ in dimension $m\geq0$. Its lower simplex is a map $K\star\Delta^m\to C$ with its final block in $\mathcal V$; its upper boundary is a map $(K\star\{0\})\star\partial\Delta^m\to C$ whose initial part is $c$. Glue these along $K\star\partial\Delta^m$. Associativity and the degreewise join formula identify the union with $K\star\partial\Delta^{m+1}$: the face without the initial post-$K$ vertex is the lower simplex, and the other faces are the upper boundary. The restriction at that initial vertex is $c$, and the final vertex is a color. The unique active maps to $[1]$ give a specified base extension $K\star\Delta^{m+1}\to B$ of its projection, as in Step 1; this construction agrees on the overlap because those same maps are unique. Apply the assumed condition with $d=m+1>0$. Its filler gives the requested $m$-simplex in $Z_c$, fixing the upper boundary and mapping to the specified lower simplex. For $m=0$ the join $\{0\}\star\partial\Delta^0$ is just the initial point and the construction glues $c$ and the prescribed $T$-cocone along $K$; thus surjectivity on vertices is included. Consequently $\psi$ is a trivial Kan fibration, and Steps 3 and 2 show that $c$ is weakly operadically colimiting. Nothing in the proof requires $K$ to have vertices: for $K=\varnothing$, the join coslices are the corresponding ambient categories and the same formulas apply. The apex $v$ was never assumed to lie over $[1]$; only the test apices $w$ were colors.

source.place: Proposition 3.1.1.7, reverse implication, including the dimension-zero lifting problem.

tool_uses.why: General relative join-coslice restriction and apex left fibrations are used to form the test map and the inner coslice projection; no coefficient or geometric theorem is used, and this unit has no substitute with this relative statement.
Only its componentwise criterion for equivalences of coherent transformations is used with space-valued transport; this is general quasicategory infrastructure.
Its isofibration assertion upgrades the already constructed left fibration to a Joyal fibration; the coefficient unit has no equivalent lifting statement.
Only the general last-edge-equivalence horn filler closes the contraction prism; it does not replace any unit-level coefficient argument.

Statement and stmt_deps are unchanged against the side-DAG base. The statement is the nonsymmetric, absolute case of HA Prop. 3.1.1.7: weakly colimiting as defined in def-coef-operadic-correspondence, d>0, tuple apex allowed, only the last test vertex a color. Because [1] is terminal in Delta^op_act, the specified base extension a is unique whenever it exists, so it is harmless. The parent kan-filling uses the item in exactly this form in its Step 3. Steps 1-3: Q is an inner fibration via relative-coslice with K0 empty. psi is a left fibration, being a pullback of rho for K in K^triangleright with target the point. The apex comparison uses: the E_w right fibration, the point into K^triangleright being right anodyne, exponentiation pulled back to c, and the join-slice fiber comparison. Fiber equivalences make psi a trivial Kan fibration via transport, the componentwise criterion, isofibration, the Joyal characterizations and the WFS, including the empty set into Delta^0. The converse is a pullback to fibers. Steps 4-7: r(W) lies in the boundary of Delta^d; I re-derived every face deletion. b_i attaches along Lambda^d_{d-i}, b_d along its full boundary, filled by psi including vertex surjectivity at d=1. s_k attaches along inner horns, and s_{d+1} along Lambda_{d+1}^{d+1}, whose last edge is degenerate and is filled by the dual outer-horn lemma.
